title: How many acute angles will the next triangle figure have?
description: Three figures are built from a growing number of small triangles. The paper corner shows that every corner of a small triangle is acute, so the acute angles are counted triangle by triangle. The check finds the same count for the next figure in two ways.
teaching_notes: One idea: every small triangle adds three acute angles, so the count is three times the number of small triangles. Watch for children who count only the corners of the big outline.

video_script.why: The child uses the paper corner to see that each small triangle has three acute angles, then spots the pattern in the counts.
video_script.substitution: The book's figures of one triangle, then four, then seven small triangles, with the paper corner laid on a corner of a small triangle.
video_script.anchor: the book's three figures: one triangle, a triangle cut into four small triangles, and a triangle cut into seven small triangles
video_script.payoff_line: The figures have three, twelve and twenty one acute angles, and the next figure has thirty. The numbers go up by nine each time.

final_answer.value: 3, 12, 21 acute angles; the next figure has 30; the numbers go up by 9 each time
final_answer.spoken: the figures have three, twelve and twenty one acute angles, and the next figure has thirty, going up by nine each time

maths_rules: every corner of a small triangle is smaller than a right angle, so each small triangle has 3 acute angles
the small triangles go 1, 4, 7, so each figure adds 3 small triangles; the next has 7 + 3 = 10, and 10 x 3 = 30
check: each new figure adds 3 x 3 = 9 acute angles, and 21 + 9 = 30
video_script.design: The three figures stay on the board and the next figure is drawn beside them. A count box under each figure fills in as the steps go on.
